connections.label: RESP TCP :6379 · replies on same socket
SET / GET / DEL · result or status

cards.title: Request and command flow
items: Four worker threads each create a non-blocking listening socket and epoll loop on TCP port 6379; SO_REUSEPORT is enabled when available.

Client bytes are accumulated and parsed as RESP arrays of bulk strings; non-array input falls back to whitespace tokenization. Incomplete commands wait for more bytes, and buffered pipelined commands are processed in sequence.
SET key value → durable SQLite write → +OK. GET key → bulk string, including a valid zero-length value, or RESP null ($-1) only when missing. DEL key → integer 1 or 0. PING → +PONG.

CONFIG GET returns hard-coded compatibility values: multi-thread=yes, maxmemory=1, appendonly=no, save='', requirepass='', timeout=0, databases=16. Unknown commands or invalid argument counts return a RESP error.

cards.title: Storage and persistence behavior
items: SQLite stores binary keys/values as BLOBs under a composite (dataset, key) primary key; datasets have separate key spaces.
Writes use SQLite WAL mode and synchronous=FULL. The API distinguishes a missing key (optional empty) from a stored empty byte sequence.
transact() applies a batch of SET/DEL mutations inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT; failures trigger rollback. Calls on one StorageEngine instance are serialized by a mutex.

Options bound dataset-name, key, and value sizes; the SQLite page cache can be limited and max_database_size_bytes caps main-database pages. This does not cap all process memory or transient WAL/backup growth.

cards.title: Concurrency and implementation technology
items: The storage core is C++17, SQLite C API, std::filesystem, and a per-instance mutex. SQLite provides transaction isolation/recovery; the service's API is still key/value, not PostgreSQL SQL.
The legacy RESP server uses POSIX sockets and epoll with four workers; it remains Linux-oriented and is not yet safe for untrusted network access.
The new CMake test target covers binary/empty values, namespace separation, transaction rollback, backup/restore, restart, and concurrent calls; native compilation still needs to be run.
CMake and vcpkg define the Windows-capable storage build. RESP/HTTP, TLS, authentication, compression, and operational metrics are not yet implemented.

cards.title: Benchmark and developer workflow
items: The Part B shell benchmark checks that localhost:6379 is reachable, then runs redis-benchmark for SET/GET.
part-b/benchmark.sh varies requests (10k, 100k, 1M), connections (10, 100, 1000), and payloads (512, 1024 bytes); results are written under results/.
The shell benchmark still drives the legacy RESP server for SET/GET; its request/connection/payload matrix is not yet a production acceptance test.
Build the SQLite storage core with root CMake + vcpkg. Existing Makefiles are legacy Linux paths. README retains the prior redis-cli and Doxygen workflow.
